sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `oh-my-pi`. [claim-oh-my-pi-product-identity]
- Canonical name: Oh My Pi, also styled `omp`. [claim-oh-my-pi-product-identity]
- Current status: the repository was not archived, showed a same-day push, and release 17.2.12 was published on 2026-08-09. [claim-oh-my-pi-repository-status] [claim-oh-my-pi-version] [claim-oh-my-pi-maintenance-signal]
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-09. [claim-oh-my-pi-product-identity]

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a local Pi-lineage agent runtime with interactive TUI, one-shot CLI, SDK, RPC, ACP, and collaboration routes. [claim-oh-my-pi-primary-type-runtime] [claim-oh-my-pi-runtime-architecture]
- What it is not: official not-for guidance was not found, so exclusions beyond proven constraints remain unknown. [claim-oh-my-pi-not-for-unknown]

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` is a project-taxonomy inference from agent-loop ownership. [claim-oh-my-pi-primary-type-runtime]
- Agent-loop owner: `@oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core` owns state, tool calls, and provider streaming through its loop implementation. [claim-oh-my-pi-agent-loop-owner]
- Architecture: one engine serves TUI, one-shot, SDK, RPC, and ACP wrappers, with a JavaScript loader and Rust N-API native layer. [claim-oh-my-pi-runtime-architecture] [claim-oh-my-pi-native-architecture]

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-tui`, `surface-oh-my-pi-one-shot`, `surface-oh-my-pi-sdk`, `surface-oh-my-pi-rpc`, `surface-oh-my-pi-acp`, `surface-oh-my-pi-collab-terminal`, `surface-oh-my-pi-collab-web`, `surface-oh-my-pi-collab-relay`, and `surface-oh-my-pi-share-viewer`. [claim-oh-my-pi-entrypoints] [claim-oh-my-pi-sdk] [claim-oh-my-pi-rpc] [claim-oh-my-pi-acp] [claim-oh-my-pi-collab] [claim-oh-my-pi-collab-web] [claim-oh-my-pi-vendor-relay] [claim-oh-my-pi-share-viewer]
- Execution location: default sessions and tools run on the same device; collab guests control or view a host-run session through a relay. [claim-oh-my-pi-local-execution] [claim-oh-my-pi-collab]
- Platform compatibility: the README documents macOS, Linux, and Windows install paths; the package manifest separately requires Bun >=1.3.14. [claim-oh-my-pi-availability] [claim-oh-my-pi-platform-compatibility]

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: role-based model routing and documented fallback chains, path-scoped sets, and credential rotation are first-party claims. [claim-oh-my-pi-model-roles] [claim-oh-my-pi-routing-fallbacks]
- Auth strategy: credential resolution spans runtime overrides, models configuration, stored OAuth/API keys, environment variables, and optional broker/gateway services. [claim-oh-my-pi-auth-precedence] [claim-oh-my-pi-auth-broker]
- Provider support: direct, gateway, custom, and keyless local-provider routes are documented; the complete live model matrix was not tested. [claim-oh-my-pi-provider-catalog] [claim-oh-my-pi-local-providers] [claim-oh-my-pi-custom-providers]

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: automatic compaction uses documented strategy and continuation settings, while exact provider-specific context limits remain unknown. [claim-oh-my-pi-compaction]
- Memory: configurable local, Hindsight, and Mnemopi memory exists but is off by default. [claim-oh-my-pi-memory]
- Compaction: compaction is a first-class session entry with manual and several automatic triggers. [claim-oh-my-pi-compaction]
- Session behavior: append-only JSONL sessions support branch-pointer navigation, fresh/clear/new/drop/fork, resume, and continue. [claim-oh-my-pi-session-storage] [claim-oh-my-pi-session-operations]

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: the README advertises a broad built-in coding tool set including file, shell, eval, LSP/debug, task, browser/computer, and memory tools. [claim-oh-my-pi-built-in-tools]
- Extensions: TypeScript/JavaScript modules can add tools, commands, shortcuts, renderers, and session actions, but run in-process. [claim-oh-my-pi-extension-model] [claim-oh-my-pi-extension-risk-drawback]
- MCP: project/user MCP configuration supports stdio, HTTP, and SSE, with trusted-input warnings. [claim-oh-my-pi-mcp-support]
- Skills: file-backed skills are discovered from several harness-compatible paths. [claim-oh-my-pi-skills-support]
- Hooks: hooks can block or rewrite tool input and replace tool results. [claim-oh-my-pi-hook-support]
- APIs: in-process SDK, NDJSON RPC, and ACP editor integration are documented. [claim-oh-my-pi-sdk] [claim-oh-my-pi-rpc] [claim-oh-my-pi-acp]

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: the task tool supports single or batched subagents, structured output, background jobs, and lifecycle control. [claim-oh-my-pi-task-orchestration]
- Parallelism: a session-scoped semaphore bounds concurrent subagents. [claim-oh-my-pi-parallelism]

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: optional task workspace isolation can return patches or branches, while extensions themselves are not sandboxed. [claim-oh-my-pi-task-isolation] [claim-oh-my-pi-extension-risk-drawback]
- Permissions: read/write/exec tiers and per-tool policies exist, with `yolo` documented as the default; headless subagents use a parent-approval boundary. [claim-oh-my-pi-approval-policy] [claim-oh-my-pi-task-orchestration]
- Security: latest-release-only, best-effort security support and optional secret obfuscation are documented. [claim-oh-my-pi-security-support] [claim-oh-my-pi-secret-obfuscation]
- Data path: default JSONL sessions live under `~/.omp/agent/sessions/<scope>-<project-basename>-<sha256(canonical-cwd)>`. [claim-oh-my-pi-session-storage] Local credentials are stored in `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` unless broker mode is active. [claim-oh-my-pi-auth-precedence] In broker mode, the broker owns the credential vault and the client keeps an encrypted snapshot cache. [claim-oh-my-pi-data-path]

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-tui` is the local interactive route with approval, tool inspection, and continuity. [claim-oh-my-pi-entrypoints] [claim-oh-my-pi-approval-policy]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-one-shot` answers one prompt and exits. [claim-oh-my-pi-entrypoints]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-sdk` and `surface-oh-my-pi-rpc` are local integration APIs. [claim-oh-my-pi-sdk] [claim-oh-my-pi-rpc]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-acp` is local IDE integration with client permission requests when effective policy requires them. [claim-oh-my-pi-acp] [claim-oh-my-pi-approval-policy]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-collab-terminal` and `surface-oh-my-pi-collab-web` join an already host-created live session through a vendor relay. [claim-oh-my-pi-collab] [claim-oh-my-pi-collab-web]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-collab-relay` records the relay transport separately from either client. [claim-oh-my-pi-vendor-relay]
- Interface and surface IDs: `surface-oh-my-pi-share-viewer` is a read-only encrypted snapshot viewer, not a live agent host. [claim-oh-my-pi-share-viewer]
- Remote behavior: collab remote control is documented, but remote start and durable remote resume remain unknown. [claim-oh-my-pi-collab] [claim-oh-my-pi-remote-start-resume-unknown]
- Mobile behavior: native mobile, first-party mobile web, and first-party messaging remain unknown; generic browser access is not promoted to mobile support. [claim-oh-my-pi-mobile-access-unknown]
- Background behavior: non-blocking task subagents can run in the background; isolated and non-isolated lifecycle rules differ. [claim-oh-my-pi-background-subagents]

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: the homepage advertises a 0 USD product offer, but provider, relay, share, quota, and hosted-service costs or terms remain unknown. [claim-oh-my-pi-pricing]
- License: MIT. [claim-oh-my-pi-license-mit]
- Maintenance: release 17.2.12 and same-day repository activity were present at capture; security support covers only the latest release. [claim-oh-my-pi-maintenance-signal] [claim-oh-my-pi-security-support]
- Lock-in: unknown; custom providers and open code do not establish full code/config migration portability. [claim-oh-my-pi-lock-in-unknown]

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: Oh My Pi explicitly calls itself a Pi fork and describes a batteries-included extension of that base. [claim-oh-my-pi-pi-fork-lineage] [claim-oh-my-pi-extends-pi]
- Relationship edges: baseline `oh-my-pi --fork_of--> pi` is preserved and not recreated; this proposal adds no relationship tuple. Added behavior remains a claim, not an `extends` edge. [claim-oh-my-pi-pi-fork-lineage] [claim-oh-my-pi-extends-pi]

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `neighborhood-pi-lineage-terminal-runtimes`. [claim-oh-my-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Substitutes: unknown; the fork relation does not prove feature or workflow parity. [claim-oh-my-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Partial substitutes: unknown pending same-user-job evidence beyond terminal positioning. [claim-oh-my-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Same-lineage relatives: Pi, Atomic, and Prime Agent; Oh My Pi's decisive differences include its batteries-included tool path, optional memory, MCP, task agents, and collab relay. [claim-oh-my-pi-lineage-neighborhood] [claim-oh-my-pi-unique-value]
- Often-confused products: unknown. [claim-oh-my-pi-lineage-neighborhood]
- Complements: unknown within an eligible Wave 1 comparison neighborhood. [claim-oh-my-pi-lineage-neighborhood]

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: vendor positioning combines a coding-first Pi fork with native tools, persistent evaluation, subagents, memory, ACP, and collab. [claim-oh-my-pi-unique-value]
- Meaningful drawbacks: unisolated extensions can fail the session, and security support is latest-release-only and best effort. [claim-oh-my-pi-extension-risk-drawback] [claim-oh-my-pi-security-support-drawback]
- Best fit: the vendor positions it for developers seeking a terminal-first, extensible coding agent. [claim-oh-my-pi-intended-user]
- Not-for: unknown; no first-party formal exclusion statement was found. [claim-oh-my-pi-not-for-unknown]
